newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert ups pressure on Boeing over McDonnell deal.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert ups pressure on Boeing over McDonnell deal.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert stepped up pressure on Boeing Co. Tuesday saying he would not accept the proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp. as it now stands.

The European Union is reviewing the merger because Boeing does a brisk business with European airlines. It has authority to impose a fine equal to 10 percent of Boeing's annual gross world income if it decides the merger is anti-competitive.

Van Miert's statement was a clear signal that he would not change his negative opinion of the deal no matter what political pressure was applied from the United States, home of the two aircraft manufacturers, EU sources said.

He also strongly rejected accusations led by U.S. Sen. Slade Gorton, R.-Wash., that the Commission was not being "objective" in its assessment of the merger and was defending the interests of Airbus Industrie -- a consortium of powerful aircraft manufacturers in France, Germany, Britain and Spain which provides the main competition for Boeing.
"Our analysis of the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas file is conducted strictly on the basis of the European merger regulation, and nothing else," he said in a statement.
Gorton of Washington, where Boeing is based, wrote to U.S. President Clinton last week urging him to ensure a fair EU review.
Boeing's vice president for EU affairs Jim Frank told Reuters he had no complaints about the way the Commission's merger task-force has been handling the case.
"So far we have not had any signs that the merger task-force would not do its work as one would expect," Frank told Reuters from Boeing's office in Brussels.
He declined to comment on the concessions sought by the Commission, but reiterated the company's belief that the deal did not dramatically change the state of competition in the aircraft industry.
